title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)', Grothendieck axiomatizes a structure he calls an 'atelier' (workshop). It is a set F of 'figures' carrying an order ≤ and a second relation ≪ (roughly 'contained in the interior of'), subject to axioms At 1–At 7. Among the figures is a set M of 'elementary figures'. For F in F, F̃ is the set of elementary figures below F (written X ◁ F on the previous page). The axioms recalled on the previous page are:
- At 1: suprema of families that are bounded above ('sup non-disjoints') exist, and F is non-empty, so it has a least element ∅_F.
- At 2: every F is the supremum of the elementary figures it majorizes.
- At 3: F ∨ G exists as soon as X ∨ Y exists for all X ◁ F and Y ◁ G. This is a local-to-global criterion for two figures to be compatible.

The previous page sets up a Galois-type bijection between 'spacious' sub-structures of F and closed parts M' of M. It sends M' to Env(M') = {F | F̃ ⊂ M'} and F' to F' ∩ M.

On this page he asks when a subset F' ⊂ F, with the induced ≤ and ≪, is again an atelier.
- At 1 and At 2 pass to F' automatically.
- At 3 needs an extra hypothesis. He imposes Sousat 1: F' is a non-empty closed part of (F, ≤). Here 'closed' must mean downward closed, a lower set or sieve.
- He also imposes Sousat 2: if F, G ∈ F' and, for all X ∈ F̃ and Y ∈ G̃, X ∨ Y exists in F' (equivalently X ∨ Y exists in F and lies in F', i.e. X and Y have a common upper bound in F'), then F ∨ G ∈ F'. By At 3 in F, F ∨ G already exists in F (he refers back to pp. 21, 27).
- He claims At 4–At 7 pass trivially to F' ('me semble-t-il').
- For At 7 he records (*): for elementary figures X, Y in M', the relation X ≪° Y holds in F if and only if it holds in F'.
- A margin note says Sousat 2 is precisely the condition At 3 for (F', ≤).

He then crosses out an attempt to view F as a sub-atelier of Fig(M), the atelier of all figures on M. Finally he defines: a sub-atelier of an atelier F is a subset F' satisfying Sousat 1 and Sousat 2. Equivalently, (1) F' is a non-empty lower set of (F, ≤), and (2) F' with the induced ≤ and ≪ is itself an atelier. The next page goes on to define 'spacious' sub-ateliers and to show that F embeds as a sub-atelier of Fig(M).

The purpose is to build the subobject theory, essentially closed subspaces, of an order-theoretic, point-free axiomatics of 'figures'. This axiomatics is aimed at a tame / combinatorial topology.
errors: The equivalence 'X ∨ Y exists in F'' ⇔ 'X, Y bounded in F'' is correct only because F' is downward closed. Then a bound Z ∈ F' gives X ∨ Y (which exists in F by At 1) ≤ Z, so X ∨ Y ∈ F'. This dependence on Sousat 1 is left implicit.

The claim that At 4–At 7 pass trivially to F' is hedged by Grothendieck himself ('me semble-t-il') and is not checked on the page. For axioms involving ≪ and an existential quantifier, a witness in F need not lie in F'; (*) only addresses the case of elementary figures in M'.
The wording is ambiguous: 'partie fermée' presumably means a lower set for ≤, but on the previous page 'fermée' also refers to closed parts of M. These are two distinct notions of closedness.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'atelier': a poset of figures with an interior relation ≪, generated by elementary figures under sups of bounded families, with a local criterion (At 3) for the existence of binary joins
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / order-theoretic topology; closest analogues are locales/frames, continuous domains (way-below relation ≪), and o-minimal or tame-topology axiomatics
ideas.usually_credited_to: Frames/locales: Ehresmann, Isbell (1972), Johnstone (1982). Way-below relation: Scott (1972), Gierz et al. Tame topology as programme: Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984).
ideas.where_published: The tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6. The 'atelier' axiomatics appears only in these 1986 Analysis situs manuscripts as far as I know.

ideas.what: Definition of sub-atelier: a non-empty lower set closed under joins whose existence is certified locally (Sousat 2), equivalently a lower set that is itself an atelier for the induced relations
ideas.modern_name: Sub-object / closed sub-locale-type notion; a 'sieve' satisfying a local gluing condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: No specific attribution; analogous to closed sublocales or downsets in domain theory

ideas.what: (*) The restriction of the elementary relation ≪° to M' is the same whether computed in F or in F'
ideas.modern_name: Induced relation is intrinsic (a full-embedding property)

missed.claim: The claim that At 4–At 7 restrict to sub-ateliers is asserted without proof and hedged. The correspondence between spacious sub-ateliers and closed parts of M (from the previous page) is left as a programme whose verification is not carried out here.
missed.quote: Les conditions At 4, At 5, At 6, At 7 passent trivialement me semble-t-il de F à F'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It is only of interest to anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 point-free 'analysis situs' axiomatics as a candidate foundation for tame topology. Comparing it with locale theory and o-minimal structures would require settling these verifications.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step: defining substructures in Grothendieck's unpublished 'atelier' axiomatics. The axiomatic project itself is little known and of some historical interest as a point-free approach to tame topology. This specific page contains only straightforward order-theoretic verifications.
transcription_corrections: Sousat 2 should read 'pour X ∈ F̃, Y ∈ G̃' (the word 'tout' is crossed out). This matches the 'X ◁ F' notation of At 3 on the previous page.
Margin note reads approximately: 'NB (!) une condition [nécessaire et suffisante?] ... : (F', ≤) ... i.e. condition At 3 pour F''. The left-margin fragment 'At 3 pour F'' is legible.
'Soit F un atelier ou un ...' is more plausibly 'Soit F un atelier, i.e. un [ensemble ordonné satisfaisant] At 1 – At 7'.
The word is clearly 'sous-atelier', not 'sous-atlas'. The next page's transcription 'sous-atlas' / 'atlas' is likely a misreading of 'sous-atelier' / 'atelier'.
'Pour At 7, je note seulement en passant' is correct. (*) uses ≪ with a small circle (≪°), written for X, Y ∈ M' (elementary figures).
